# Testing Timer in Shinylive

This is a minimal test to prove timers work in Shinylive.

```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| viewerHeight: 600

library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  titlePanel("Timer Test - Should Update Every Second"),

  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      h4("Controls"),
      actionButton("start_sim", "Start 10-Second Task", class = "btn-primary"),
      hr(),
      h4("Current Time (updates every 100ms):"),
      verbatimTextOutput("clock"),
      h4("Task Progress:"),
      verbatimTextOutput("progress")
    ),

    mainPanel(
      h4("Simulation Output"),
      plotOutput("test_plot"),
      hr(),
      tags$div(
        style = "font-size: 11px; color: #666;",
        paste("Dashboard created:", format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S UTC"))
      )
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  # Reactive values
  task_state <- reactiveVal("idle")
  task_start <- reactiveVal(NULL)
  task_progress <- reactiveVal(0)

  # Reactive timer - updates every 100ms
  autoInvalidate <- reactiveTimer(100)

  # Clock display - ALWAYS updates to prove timer works
  output$clock <- renderText({
    autoInvalidate()  # Trigger every 100ms
    format(Sys.time(), "%H:%M:%S.%OS1")  # Show milliseconds
  })

  # Progress display
  output$progress <- renderText({
    autoInvalidate()  # Check every 100ms

    if (task_state() == "running") {
      elapsed <- difftime(Sys.time(), task_start(), units = "secs")
      progress_pct <- min(100, as.numeric(elapsed) * 10)  # 10 second task

      sprintf("Status: RUNNING\nElapsed: %.1f seconds\nProgress: %.0f%%",
              as.numeric(elapsed), progress_pct)
    } else if (task_state() == "complete") {
      "Status: COMPLETE\nTask finished!"
    } else {
      "Status: IDLE\nClick button to start"
    }
  })

  # Start button handler
  observeEvent(input$start_sim, {
    task_state("running")
    task_start(Sys.time())
    task_progress(0)

    # Simulate 10-second task with chunked execution
    for (i in 1:10) {
      Sys.sleep(1)  # Sleep 1 second
      task_progress(i * 10)

      # In real dashboard, update reactive values here
      # This simulates what should happen during simulation
    }

    task_state("complete")
  })

  # Plot output
  output$test_plot <- renderPlot({
    if (task_state() == "idle") {
      plot(1, type = "n", main = "Waiting to start...")
    } else if (task_state() == "running") {
      # This should update during task
      invalidateLater(500)  # Refresh plot every 500ms
      prog <- task_progress()
      barplot(prog, ylim = c(0, 100), main = paste("Progress:", prog, "%"),
              col = "steelblue")
    } else {
      barplot(100, ylim = c(0, 100), main = "Complete!",
              col = "green")
    }
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

## Expected Behavior

1. **Clock**: Should update every 100ms showing current time with milliseconds
2. **Progress**: Should show elapsed time and percentage during task
3. **Plot**: Should update showing progress bar

## If This Works

Then the timer pattern is correct and the issue is elsewhere in the main dashboard.

## If This Doesn't Work

Then WebR/Shinylive has a fundamental limitation with timers.
